chapter: Chicago, the Woodside, the army and 52nd Street
title: Lester Young's earthy wisdom and Chin Chow sayings
summary: Prez was a profound man with earthy sayings, clipped Chin Chow's maxims daily, and expressed himself like no one else.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: But Prez was a very -- he was a very earthy man. He had earthy sayings, very profound sayings, very profound man. You know, he could say things that would really hit home, but they were really home sayings. You know, they weren't very -- what can I say intellectual or something, but really, really hit --
Mother wit, that was it. He was a very profound man and --
Do you remember anything like that, examples?

No, I can't just cite, you know, anything in particular. But he loved Chin Chow. You remember in the paper they had this little Chinaman, I think it's a Chinaman, Chin Chow says this, and all of these sayings like Confusius, you know. Prez lived by this, every day he would cut this out and it was just some profound sayings. But he had an earthy way about him that was -- Lester -- no one else, there was no one like Lester, no one could express himself like Lester.
